title: Advancement in graphene-based anode materials for high-performance sodium-ion batteries
content: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) have emerged as an alternative for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) in energy storage applications, because of their similar electrochemical performance, abundance of sodium resources, and low cost. However, compared to lighter and smaller Li+, the heavier mass and bigger radius of Na+ lead to lower electrochemical kinetics and larger volume expansion of active materials. Graphene-based anode materials demonstrate improved and diverse properties for SIBs in terms of high-rate capability, flexible-battery structures, high specific capacity and long cycling life due to their unique characteristics such as high theoretical capacity, high electronic conductivity, great mechanical strength, high charge carrier mobility, and large surface area. Moreover, when combined with other nanomaterials in electrodes, graphene can enhance electrical conductivity, control large volume changes, and accelerate reaction kinetics. The article addresses the latest developments in the application of graphene-based anodes for SIBs, emphasizing their characteristics, fabrication process, sodium storage technique, and electrochemical performance. In order to improve the sodium storage performance of graphene-based electrodes, challenges, and strategies for improving anode performance are also discussed.
